reviews.text: RUN RABBIT RUN will follow me around like a shadow. It is going to take a while for me to shake this one.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: The Australian film does a neat job in creating an atmospheric horror but loses its command over the genre after a point.
reviews.author: Srivatsan S

reviews.text: The film rests squarely on the shoulders of Succession star Snook, who does a lot of heavy lifting, keeping us sympathetic right up to, and maybe even beyond, the point of revelation. parenthood.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: After all the metaphors and horror tropes, Reid’s Run Rabbit Run is an undercooked supernatural film which had the potential to bring new ideas. However, it resulted in a missed opportunity to tell a story on the trauma and grief of motherhood.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run could have benefitted from a tighter and more precise screenplay but instead meanders to an unsatisfactory conclusion that audiences most likely predicted before it happened, rendering the chill of it lukewarm at best.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: An Australian dark psychological thriller.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Sarah Snook does the best she can with the poor material given to her, but it isn’t enough.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run really attempts to lean into the psychological horror of its plot and gives more patience to its grieving characters, which is admirable on a conceptual level. If only there was more patience to spare for its lack of original ideas.
reviews.author: Anna Miller

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run is a very stale and unimaginative horror flick that has repetitive and boring scenes of a mother hallucinating and having a bad temper. The story's 'mystery secret' (revealed at the end) is too easy to solve, so there's hardly any suspense.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Hannah Kent’s script keeps us guessing to the end, and the atmospherically tricksy story is much enhanced by juvenile thespian LaTorre’s precociously eerie performance.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: There are clichés all over the shop, but they’re deployed with skill and precision, making this small-scale effort a cut above bigger efforts, such as the latest Insidious movie. Very good stuff.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: This is a creepy and disturbing Australian horror movie that's a reflection on life and death, grieving and trauma.
reviews.author: Brian Costello

reviews.text: This Australian psychological thriller. starring Sarah Snook,  is fearful yet frustrating - an eerie, minimalist glimpse into guilt and motherhood but the conflicted characters & backstory are not sufficiently developed to emotionally engage the audience.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run has strong individual moments of terror, but the film never comes together satisfyingly enough.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: Led by powerful performances, but wastes its “creepy kid” premise by playing its cards too close to the chest.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run doesn’t fall behind by being a collection of clichés, but more that it takes the same old scenario and stretches it long and thin.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run plays as another riff on trauma, using The Babadook as a key outline. The difference comes in the form of just how aggravating it is to watch less accomplished filmmaking.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: If it’s not scary, what’s the point?
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: While it definitely won’t win any awards for originality, relative newcomers to mummy mayhem should find an hour and 40 minutes of ghoulish distraction here.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: A psychological thriller that’s mostly effective, even though its story is familiar and somewhat threadbare.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: While not a complete failure, Run Rabbit Run is ultimately not really worth a watch, unless you’re a Sarah Snook fan or a psychological horror newbie.
reviews.author: Symphony Barnes

reviews.text: Not everything works here. Too much is overfamiliar. But Run Rabbit Run retains a clammy grip throughout.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: This is an well-made thriller about ghosts – of the past and present – that keeps one guessing until the end, and perhaps even afterwards.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Daina Reid’s Australian thriller Run Rabbit Run is yet another tired slab of trauma horror seemingly aimed at audiences unfamiliar with such exotic concepts as allegory and metaphor.
reviews.author: Steven Warner

reviews.text: A little less than the sum of its parts, Run Rabbit Run is ultimately more intriguing than outright terrifying.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Such inconsistency is usually a dealbreaker, unless you’ve got someone who can guide you through the dead space and past the rough patches -- and this is where Snook comes in.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Reid foregoes bloodshed for scary unseen things, directs with confidence and a strong cinematographic eye... But the material ends up tripping over too many tropes to be a deeper excursion into the psychology of childhood and motherhood.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: This is the older kind of thriller, the kind that uses secrets and boiling anger as its currency.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: “Run Rabbit Run” is intended as a slow burn, but it’s mostly slow and little burn.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Just one of Shiv’s frosty, cunning glances is more scary and original than anything Run Rabbit Run has to offer.
reviews.author: Eliza Janssen

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run is less than the sum of its parts, and even an excellent turn from Sarah Snook can't elevate the movie beyond its basest instincts.
reviews.author: Graeme Guttmann

reviews.text: The film is a little overly fond of its own feints and sleights of hand — editing crescendos, drones on the soundtrack — but summons a palpable sense of disquiet, thanks to Snook’s unnerving performance as a mother unravelling...
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Overall, Run Rabbit Run is a disappointing addition to the horror space, saturated with repetitive, bland material that fails to build the momentum it seeks.
reviews.author: Emma Vine

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run never gets past the sensation of being a Mad Libs horror movie, where those blank spaces are filled in with the most obvious tropes.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run is unable to maintain the momentum from its chilling buildup because the story becomes uninteresting almost immediately. Our two leads are great, but the pacing falls completely flat.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Kent’s script relies too heavily on standard horror tropes that are repetitive.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Its repetitiveness and lack of narrative momentum keeps things stuck in neutral.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Netflix’s new horror original makes the irredeemable sin of wasting Sarah Snook.
reviews.author: Alex Welch

reviews.text: A bundle of cheap and loud jump scares with equally obnoxious characters, even if the solid performers are trying to make the most of this messy mass hysteria
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: This comes across as a horror film made by a talented director who clearly loves the genre but couldn’t find a truly original path for this particular tale.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Gloomy and vague, Run Rabbit Run is a moody, noncommittal tease replete with the usual spectral signifiers... Snook does everything but rend her garments in a performance that only emphasizes the busy vapidity of Hannah Kent’s script.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: “Run Rabbit Run” is a solid, spooky tale without anything too flashy like a Babadook to haunt our dreams and memes but chilling enough to make us sit up in our chairs and scan the screen for the next sign of danger.
reviews.author: Monica Castillo

reviews.text: Even though Sarah Snook gives a complex performance as a struggling mother who doesn’t understand what’s happening with her daughter, the story falls flat.
reviews.author: Amanda Guarragi

reviews.text: You kind of know how Run Rabbit Run is going to pan out, with only Snook’s deft handling of her character’s descent into mania saving this from completely derailing into an unwatchable mess.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: It succeeds as an unsettling, sad and – at several moments – horribly chilling meditation on motherhood, loss and the spectres of the past.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Gregory

reviews.text: The story certainly doesn’t break new ground, and given the modest nature of the movie, there’s a bit of impatience to get where it’s going; still, thanks to Snook and LaTorre’s beyond-her-years performance it’s never less than watchable.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run has a solid but simple premise, yet the performances of its leads make this grief-stricken yet guilty story last after the credits roll.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Despite the talent involved, Run Rabbit Run ends up being a dull trudge through familiar horror tropes.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: [D]irector Daina Reid's psychological thriller ... just spins in circles until it finally reveals what is actually happening...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Horror movies that tackle mental illness and family tension still need to deliver the horror, but Run Rabbit Run comes off as a dull, meandering therapy session.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Isn’t an aggressive genre experience, but something more sinister, supported by active performances and a distinct conclusion to make the journey worthwhile.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: So indebted to its forebears that it feels derivative by default.
reviews.author: Michael Sun

reviews.text: This psychological horror, with a chilling atmosphere similar to "Babadook" or "Hereditary", will make you question your sanity until the predictable yet impressive ending.
reviews.author: Zofia Wijaszka

reviews.text: Even Sarah Snook can’t redeem this derivative Aussie horror
reviews.author: Leila Latif

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run bridges the fantastical or imaginary and the horror of being human.
reviews.author: Paul Risker

reviews.text: It’s Snook’s performance, one that starts off more contained but grows bigger by the minute all the way up to the highwire finale, that draws you in.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: Sarah Snook and especially Lily LaTorre (who will go onto much better things) try their best to carry Run Rabbit Run on their shoulders. However, without any ingenuity in its horror elements and compelling drama in its story, it is unfortunately a bust.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: The gothic ghost story vibe of this film is nuanced and many-layered; chilling scenes of terror are created without resorting to jump scares or special effects.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: Reid’s handsomely shot film takes its time building to its inevitable climax, and some of the more familiar genre tropes feel a little on the nose. But Snook carries the piece with gusto...
reviews.author: Ed Gibbs

reviews.text: “Run Rabbit Run” has a patience that sets it apart from the standard-issue horror fare we’ve grown accustomed to. It leans into the psychological aspect of its story as it examines a range of familiar themes, some better defined than others.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: "Run Rabbit Run" engages in the worst impulses in horror storytelling, conjuring scare scenes that barely add nervous momentum.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: Reid keeps things super scary, and Snook's rich, perplexing performance keeps us on our toes right until the very frightening ending.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: A psychological thriller that feels as if it grows bored with itself. Using tired genre tropes and a skimpy story, the movie is akin to treading water for 90 minutes and getting nowhere.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: You can have a great lead performance, but if the film struggles to maintain momentum in its pacing and doesn’t quite know how to handle its disturbing subject matter, it’s hard to be emotionally invested, let alone scared.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run not only fails in cashing in on a haunting performance by Sarah Snook but ultimately is a cinematic chore running in place for 90 minutes.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run ends up a bit too scattershot for its own good.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Ultimately, the film feels like a missed opportunity to explore the ways childhood never really leaves us, and how having children can force a mother to question who she really is.
reviews.author: Jourdain Searles

reviews.text: Exquisite tension and atmosphere for the first 40 minutes, but like so many horror films, it loses steam by the end.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: With the ideas it brings, you’ll be excited to see what lies before you once you get through the maze. But there’s so much 'Run Rabbit Run' wants to show you about this story, where the ultimate conclusion might seem like a letdown.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Not The Babadook clone that the synopsis might hint at, Run Rabbit Run has its own identity, but does still fall foul of being a tad too formulaic.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: Australian horror thriller Run Rabbit Run starts out as a pleasingly familiar creepy kid yarn, but it runs out of gas very quickly en route to becoming ploddingly tedious.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Director Daina Reid does a great job visualizing this lifting of the veil with figures hiding in shadows while young LaTorre steals scenes opposite an unraveling Snook with uncanny ease.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The origins of all this unstable melodrama eventually unfold, but outside of its primary performances, this dark fable provides little meat to chew on.
reviews.author: Michael Frank

reviews.text: A chilling and well-executed horror with outstanding performances and haunting cinematography.
reviews.author: Michael Levine

reviews.text: It lacks outright scares and novelty but makes up for it in some psychological depth.
reviews.author: Alex Saveliev

reviews.text: ‘Run Rabbit Run’ has plenty of atmosphere, but jarring and undercooked similarities to ‘The Babadook,’ —another unsettling meditation on motherhood —end up skinning it of all potential.
reviews.author: Josh Korngut

reviews.text: Despite a phenomenal performance from Sarah Snook, Run Rabbit Run struggles to be consistently thrilling, with repetitive scenes that cause the second act to drag. Still, its heavy final act will stick with you.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: Reid and Kent suitably ratchet up the tension and suspense as required by the genre ... They even manage to throw in a few shocks and scares that even the most experienced and/or jaded horror fan won’t see coming until its far too late.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: The family mystery is rather obvious and anticlimactic. Snook is as powerful as ever portraying a mother pushed to her limits, but it's not enough to recommend the film.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run drains its characters of any compelling arc or personality, leaving you to wonder why you should care about the predictable mystery or the one-note family dynamics.
reviews.author: Jessica Scott

reviews.text: Reed, writer Hanna Kent and actor Snook form a tight troika, layering Run Rabbit Run slowly – perhaps too slowly – to the point where it’s easy to forget that the framework is recognisable.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: ...in its conclusion (Run Rabbit Run) tumbles over the edge, opting for ambiguity and uncertainty rather than a defined conclusion, making this an unsatisfying mystery that I cannot heartily recommend.
reviews.author: Andrew F. Peirce

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run wasn't a homerun for me personally but as a psychological horror, it covers all the bases.
reviews.author: Jonathan DeHaan

reviews.text: While Sarah Snook does all she can to give the experience some heft, Run Rabbit Run is a horror film in search of something greater others have already achieved that it is never able to find.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run’s final act lands with more of a thud than the desired bang.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: It's becoming almost a trope in itself for modern horror to revolve around trauma and grief and... Run Rabbit Run sinks into forgettable territory
reviews.author: Kevin Wight

reviews.text: I was... happily sandwiched between two friends whose nervous giggles, along with Snook’s characteristically arresting performance, were more than enough to keep me in my seat.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: There are nuggets of a better film here, but what we have is an undercooked mystery with little atmosphere, leaving us with a final product that is, quite frankly, just plain boring.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run makes the unfortunate decision to stick to its philosophy of less is more. As a result, everything suffers, and there is no real catharsis for the audience or the characters.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: The psychological thriller keeps you on the edge of your seat. The focus is on mother-daughter relationships while sins of the past play a role in Daina Reid’s chiller with memorable performances by Sarah Snook and newcomer Lily LaTorre.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: What it lacks in thrills it makes up for in a pair of compelling lead performances, despite a frustrating end.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run survives (just barely) on the strength of Sarah Snook's increasingly deranged performance... strong supporting work from Lily LaTorre is also an asset.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Sarah Snook’s commanding performance keeps this boilerplate horror film watchable, even if it largely cribs from prior, superior genre offerings.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Defies cynical expectations as another slow-burn horror movie in that it pays off.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: What it lacks in thematic newness, “Run Rabbit Run” makes up for in the sophistication of its moment-to-moment scarifying and its performances from Sarah Snook and outstanding newcomer Lily LaTorre...
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run is a pile-up of banal horror tropes. Director of photography Bonnie Elliott conjures some sweepingly foreboding images of the Australian landscape, even when working with a drone camera, but there’s something sleepy about the whole affair.
reviews.author: Ryan Lattanzio

reviews.text: Despite a solid performance from Sarah Snook (“Succession”), this Sundance midnight selection remains more of a premise than a fully fleshed-out feature.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run rests on the strong performances of Snook, LaTorre, and one ever-present white bunny.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Sanity And Tension Dwindle In This Australian Psychological Thriller.
reviews.author: Erin Brady

reviews.text: Run Rabbit Run is a substandard horror drama that underwhelms on both the chills and the emotional punch.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

synopsis: As a fertility doctor, Sarah has a firm understanding of the cycle of life. However, when she is forced to make sense of the increasingly strange behavior of her young daughter, Sarah must challenge her own beliefs and confront a ghost from her past.
